Okay, before I rant, I must establish my background: several years ago, i was in a very serious accident and sustained a traumatic brain injury as a result. When I initially began therapy, I could not use a knife and fork and felt humiliated to have to eat predominantly with my hands Balance was difficult. Over the years, with tons of support and love from many sources and wonderful therapists, I have regained some function (also thanks to people who turned me onto brain healthy eating!) I know the damage is still there, but because I was fairly young when the damage occurred, neural plasticity was possible and I know that is a big reason why I have progressed from where I was years ago. I am still not where I was before, but I am not where I was back when the injury first happened, and I have a lot of gratitude for that. So with that said, on with the rant...

I attend an aerobics/yoga hybrid class that is held expressly for people with "limitations." Oh, and that for her goal "she wants to just break a sweat." (Haven't the disabled suffered enough?) So...okay. We're going through the paces and the instructor sees me with my foot in the air and counts off 5 with me and starts clapping and says "Everybody, Jagz hit her goal" and they do the come over and applaud thing. And I could kind of felt a vein pop because I hate, HATE that - you struggle with balance because you have mutilated yourself to an extent to where your center of gravity is off - I struggle with balance because a car slammed into me and smashed my brain against my skull. Now, do not get me wrong, I value every day and am not depressed about this, but it's just the truth. HOW DARE you equate yourself to people like us. I just looked her like she had two heads.
